alt: DHCS 6251 (Revised 11/2021), Medi-Cal Estate Recovery Questionnaire, used to determine whether estate recovery applies to a deceased beneficiary's assets.
summary: Form DHCS 6251 (Rev. 11/2021) is the official Medi-Cal Estate Recovery Questionnaire submitted to the Department of Health Care Services. In accordance with California Probate Code Sections 215, 9202, and 19202, a notice of death must be provided to DHCS to determine if estate recovery applies and to identify potential hardship or statutory exceptions.
keywords: California Department of Health Care Services
full_text:
DHCS 6251 (Revised 11/2021) Page 1 of 2
State of California—Health and Human Services Agency
Department of Health Care Services
 MEDI-CAL ESTATE RECOVERY 
QUESTIONNAIRE
Notice of death must be provided to the Department of Health Care Services pursuant to California law (Probate Code Sections 215, 9202, and 19202).
Please complete this form and mail it to the address below:
Department of Health Care Services
Third Party Liability and Recovery Division 
Recovery Branch, MS 4720
PO Box 997425
Sacramento, CA 95899-7425
Please complete this questionnaire to the best of your knowledge. Include a copy of the decedent’s death certificate. We will contact you if we have any additional questions.
Decedent’s Name:
Social Security Number:
Date of Birth:
Date of Death:
1. Will the estate be probated?
Yes No If yes, enter the probate number:
County of filing: Total estimated value of probated assets:
If applicable, provide a copy of the Letters of Administration and Inventory and Appraisal.
2. Check any of the following that apply:
Decedent’s spouse or registered domestic partner is still living.
Decedent is survived by a child under the age of 21, as of the date of death.
Decedent is survived by a child of any age who is blind or disabled.
3. Is there property that is on or near a federally recognized reservation, Pueblo, or Colony?
